bracket: [Textbook misprint: the data table heads its two concentration columns \(\mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}\ s^{-1}}\), but a concentration cannot carry \(\mathrm{s^{-1}}\); the correct unit for both is \(\mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}\). Only the third column, the initial rate, is per second. The answer is unaffected, because the derivation uses only the ratios of the tabulated values.]

[Textbook misprint: the book prints the final unit as \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}\), which contradicts its own substitution one line above — \((\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}) / (\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}})^2\) gives \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}\ L\ s^{-1}}\), with \(L\) to the power \(+1\). The unit has been corrected here so the worked example does not teach the wrong dimensions for a second order rate constant; the value \(1.625\) is as printed and is correct.]

[Textbook misprint: the last line prints the units as \(\mathrm{J/mol^{-1}}\) and \(\mathrm{kJ/mol^{-1}}\), which invert "per mole" twice; they should read \(\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}\) and \(\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) (equivalently \(\mathrm{J/mol}\) and \(\mathrm{kJ/mol}\)). The numerical result \(98.8\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) is correct.]

[Textbook misprint: the book writes the temperature-dependence relation with \(2.303\,RT\) in the denominator, where \(2.303\,R\) belongs — the temperature is already carried by the bracket \((T_2 - T_1)/T_1T_2\). The chapter's own Eq. (6.23) prints \(E_a/(2.303\,R)\), and this example's own substitution divides by \(2.303 \times 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}mol^{-1}}\) with no \(T\), which is what gives its printed \(2.212\). The formula has been corrected here; the printed answer \(1.464 \times 10^{5}\) min is correct.]

[Textbook misprint: step (i) is printed as \(\mathrm{2\,ClO^{-} \longrightarrow ClO_2^{\ominus}}\), which is not balanced — two chlorine atoms enter and one leaves. The step intended is \(\mathrm{2\,ClO^{\ominus} \longrightarrow ClO_2^{\ominus} + Cl^{\ominus}}\), which balances and which, added to step (ii), reproduces the overall equation given. The answer is unaffected: \(\mathrm{ClO_2^{\ominus}}\) is the species formed in step (i) and consumed in step (ii) under either reading.]

[Textbook misprint: the rate law is printed as rate \(= k[\mathrm{NO_2}]^2[\mathrm{Cl_2}]\), but the reaction given contains no \(\mathrm{NO_2}\) at all; the intended concentration term is \([\mathrm{NO}]^2\). The answer is unaffected, since the question asks what \(k\) depends on and no concentration term appears in \(k\).]

[Textbook misprint: the organic product is printed as \(\mathrm{CH_3OH^{\ominus}}\), carrying a negative charge. Methanol is a neutral molecule, so the product should be \(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\); as printed the equation also does not balance in charge. The rate law and the answer are unaffected.]

[Textbook misprint: the relation is printed as \(\log_{10} k = 14.34 - 1.25 \times 10^{4}\ T\), with the division sign dropped. As printed, \(\log_{10}k\) would be linear in \(T\) itself rather than in \(1/T\), which is not the Arrhenius form and yields no activation energy at all; the coefficient would also carry the wrong dimensions. The intended relation is \(\log_{10} k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^{4}}{T}\), and the book's own printed answer of \(239.3\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\) is what that reading gives. The solution below uses it.]
